rules_evaluated.evidence: M2 sequencing stays in this module file's own Next (65-66) and Pre-reads (68-78) sections; the linked lecture bodies carry no module numbering.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This target is a coordinating module file; its structural headings and room-framing slides are owned by the slides class. Linked lecture files own their own concept-header judgments.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's BODY is size-bounded, not just its header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Slide-body density is owned by the slides class and the slide-size gate, not the storytelling-class placement check.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go; forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The module file itself contains no student-copied prompt fences or prompt-registry markers. Its forcing functions live in the four linked exercise files, evaluated at exercise scope.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm checked: authored pause/comparison cues can make self-study incoherent and substitute a script for trainer judgment. That harm is absent -- lines 22-34 state an upfront room agreement with no timed pause, pair activity, or comparison cue. The fast-operator persona's read exposes a DIFFERENT, non-harmful fact about this same design choice: because the recovery for the operator's skim risk (the Meta block's named 'technical warm-up' diagnosis + trainer push-back line) correctly lives outside body text per this rule, that persona never sees it. This is the rule working as designed, not a violation of it -- flagged in the persona confusions as context for the trainer, not as a rule finding.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-exercise leap test -- 3 observable Monday outcomes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The module-level leap test at lines 132-135 names three observable outcomes with falsifiers (deliberate /context use, a failing test written before the fix, a CLAUDE.local.md rule tied to a quoted session moment). All three personas' close-state artifacts satisfy the falsifiers, including the fast-operator persona whose PR still ships tests-first even though its Ex3/Ex4 scrutiny is thinner.

The table at lines 146-159 pairs every named forcing function with a dominant failure mode and a trainer-delivered recovery move. This run's fast-operator persona independently reproduced two of the table's own named failure modes ('Ex3 rules rubber-stamp', 'Ex4 rule rubber-stamp') from a cold skim-first read, which is direct evidence the table is priced against a real reader, not a hypothetical one.

Audience triangle: mid-layer-competent 9/9 (phase/close), opinionated-senior 8/8, fast-operator 7/7. All three clear the 7-floor; the mid-layer and senior reads land above the facilitator-premium line while the fast-operator lands exactly at it. Disagreement is real and reported, not averaged: the senior persona's mood is carried entirely by Ex1/Ex3/Ex4 (the process framing at lines 22-34 doesn't move him either direction), while the fast-operator's mood is measurably lower because that same framing -- read at skim speed -- fails to install the priming Ex2's payoff depends on, exactly matching the Meta block's own named drift risk ('this is just a TDD fix I do anyway'). Setup beats (room agreement, freedom-to-choose) are compressible into a parenthetical without breaking the orient-fix-close-compound arc, so the mood floor doesn't bind them structurally -- but the fast-operator trace shows that even a mood-exempt setup beat has real downstream cost for a skim-first reader when it's the vehicle carrying priming for a later teaching beat.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: No REVISE-level defect: the module's own Meta block already diagnoses this exact persona's risk and hands the trainer a named recovery line, and rule 27 correctly keeps that recovery out of body text. Worth a maintainer note only if a future pass wants a stronger self-signaling opener for self-study delivery, where no trainer voice exists to catch the drift live.

rules_evaluated.evidence: The self-report Key Concepts bullet (line 59) reads 'Read it as the agent's account of the repo, not the repo. Introspection generates hypotheses; the artifact rules' -- epistemic across all three persona reads, none of whom register it as adversarial or shame-flavored. The matching LO at line 17 ('Distinguish the agent's account of your repo from the repo's actual state') reads the same way.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The Big Idea at line 6 states the positive stake first ('leave something behind the next session can use') and names the failure mode only as the contrastive second sentence. All three personas registered this framing (mid-layer and senior explicitly; the fast-operator persona registered only the headline word 'compounding' at skim speed, which is a persona-specific reading-depth finding, not a rule violation -- the discipline-first structure is present in the text regardless of how fast a given reader takes it in).

Strategy doc's M1 order (orient, fix, close, compound, then the two recognition closers) matches the module file's link order at lines 44-54 for every persona's read. No plan-mode teaching or Skill invocation appears in any persona's trace. The Next section (65-66) hands cleanly to M2's plan-mode depth without any persona's read surfacing early exposure to that mechanism -- including the fast-operator persona, whose skim doesn't accidentally pick up M2 material either.

mood_summary.triangle_note: Disagreement is the finding, not noise. Mid-layer and senior both clear ship-bar-and-above by different routes (senior's mood is earned entirely by Ex1/Ex3/Ex4, unassisted by the room-framing beats). Fast-operator lands exactly at the facilitator-premium floor (7), not below it -- the module's own Meta block names this persona's exact risk ('mood drift toward technical warm-up') and prices the recovery as a trainer-delivered push-back line, consistent with rule 27's body/trainer split. No persona fell below 7, so nothing here is blocking; the fast-operator read is reported in full because it is the persona most likely to walk this file in the wild.
